title: Distributed Web Crawler
question: Design a distributed web crawler that fetches billions of web pages. How do you handle URL politeness, deduplication, and scaling?

rubric.name: requirements_scale
rubric.description: Estimates throughput (pages/sec), storage per page, and freshness update frequency.

rubric.name: frontier_politeness_design
rubric.description: Architects URL Frontier with host-based delay queues to respect `robots.txt` and prevent DDoS on target sites.

rubric.name: deduplication_storage
rubric.description: Uses Bloom Filters or Fingerprinting (SimHash) for URL and content duplicate detection.

rubric.name: distributed_worker_scaling
rubric.description: Scales worker nodes, handles worker crashes, DNS resolution caching, and HTML parser isolation.

rubric.name: observability_monitoring
rubric.description: Monitors dead links, trap cycles (infinite dynamic URLs), spider traps, and network errors.

expected_signals: Explains URL Frontier with FIFO queue + host queue for politeness
Uses Bloom Filter for fast URL deduplication in memory
Caches DNS queries locally to prevent DNS bottleneck
red_flags: Crawls target servers continuously without delay or robots.txt compliance
Uses relational DB lookup for every single URL duplicate check
follow_up_prompts: How do you detect and break out of infinite spider traps like dynamically generated calendar links?
How would you store and update web page checksums for duplicate content detection?
